space.description: 'model' (design space, US survey feet) or a sheet id/name (paper space, inches), e.g. 'SH-004' or 'P-201'

boundary_layers.description: with at: trace only linework on these layers

commands.name: draw_traverse
commands.description: Draw lines and curves by bearing and distance (COGO), the way a deed, a field book or a design report gives them: start at a point -- or at the end of an entity, to carry on from it -- and run course after course, each a quadrant bearing, an azimuth or a deflection from the previous course, and a distance; a curve course by radius, turn and delta, length or chord. The engine computes every point, so there is no trigonometry to do by hand, and close=true reports how well a boundary closes (precision 1:N). The traverse query computes the same points without drawing.

space.description: 'model' (design space, US survey feet) or a sheet id/name (paper space, inches), e.g. 'SH-004' or 'P-201'

layer.description: layer name; defaults to the current layer

start.description: where the traverse begins: a point [x, y] (x = easting, y = northing), or an entity id to continue from its end (start_at says which end; the entity's direction there is the course a leading deflection turns from)

start_at.description: with a start entity: continue from its end (default) or its start

items.description: one course. Straight: a direction (exactly one of bearing, azimuth, deflection, angle_right) and distance. Curve: radius, turn and one of delta, length or chord; it continues the previous course's direction unless chord_bearing places it (a non-tangent curve). Or the course as text: "N 47°30'15\" E 250", "AZ 75.5 250", "33 L 820", "CURVE R=450 LEFT DELTA=33"

bearing.description: quadrant bearing: N 47°30'15" E, S47-30-15W, N47E

azimuth.description: degrees clockwise from north, 0-360 (a number or DMS text)

deflection.description: the angle turned from the previous course, with its side: '33 L', '18°30'00" RT', or a number with right (clockwise) positive; or its size with turn

turn.description: which way a deflection or a curve turns

angle_right.description: angle measured clockwise from the backsight (the previous course run backwards), as a field traverse records it

distance.description: length of a straight course (feet in model)

radius.description: radius of a curve course -- giving one makes the course a curve

chord_bearing.description: a non-tangent curve's chord bearing (or azimuth)

legs.description: the courses in order, each from where the last one ended

initial_bearing.description: the direction a leading deflection or tangent curve turns from, as a quadrant bearing

close.description: the traverse should close on its start: report the misclosure (distance, bearing, precision 1:N) and, when drawing, add the closing course

polyline.description: draw one polyline instead of separate lines (straight courses only; with close it is a closed polyline)

ord: place line by bearing and distance

commands.name: place_callout
commands.description: Text with a leader pointing at something: the way a drafter annotates geometry that carries no design model of its own -- a pavement edge, a utility, anything seen through a reference. Name what it points at: target_entity (an id from find_entities or hit_test, referenced entities included) or target_anchor (a station, offset or named point of an alignment, a referenced one included). Plan callouts belong on the sheet, and from a sheet both are seen through its viewport -- the tip lands in paper inches where the model shows, with no scale or twist arithmetic to do by hand. Leader, landing, arrowhead and text are drawn as ordinary entities on the current or given layer.

space.description: 'model' (design space, US survey feet) or a sheet id/name (paper space, inches), e.g. 'SH-004' or 'P-201'

layer.description: layer name; defaults to the current layer

target.description: an explicit point for the leader to point at, in the callout's own space (paper inches on a sheet); prefer target_entity or target_anchor, which cannot miss

target_entity.description: what to point at, by id (find_entities and hit_test return them; reference elements are 'BASE:LN-017'). The engine computes a point on it, so a curve is aimed at correctly. On a sheet it may be a model or referenced entity: the tip lands where the viewport shows it. Give exactly one of target / target_entity / target_anchor.

at.description: where along target_entity the leader TIP goes: start|mid|end or a fraction 0-1 (default mid) -- not where the text goes, which is position. From a sheet it runs along the part of the entity that sheet shows, so mid is always a point the reader can see

target_anchor.description: a station, offset or named point of an alignment to point at: '87+41.62@19.75L', 'PC-2', {station, offset}. There is no entity at a station, so this is how a station-and-offset callout is aimed

alignment.description: the alignment target_anchor is on; a referenced one is 'BASE:RTE-7' (read, not owned -- the callout carries no anchor). Defaults to the document's only alignment

viewport.description: on a sheet, the viewport to see the target through (default: the first one that shows it)

position.description: where the text sits, clear of the geometry, in the callout's own space. The text reads away from the target: when the target is to the left, the text starts here and runs right (left-justified); when it is to the right, the text ends here (right-justified). Vertically it is centred on this point, and the landing runs from here back toward the target

content.description: the callout's text; \n starts a new line

height.description: text height in space units (feet in model, inches on sheets); defaults to the annotation scale in model space, 0.10 in on a sheet

landing.description: horizontal shoulder at the text (default 2.5 x height; 0 for none)

commands.name: place_dimension
commands.description: Measure the drawing and say so on it: linear, aligned, angular, radius, diameter or arc_length. The document stores the measurement -- the points, the arc, and where the dimension line was dragged to -- and derives extension lines, dimension line, arrowheads and the number from it, so the text cannot drift from the geometry and the annotation scale re-sizes the annotation without moving the measurement. Name what to measure (of_entity for one entity end to end or a curve's own geometry, from_entity/to_entity for two, two lines for the angle between them) or give the points outright; line_point settles which measurement was meant.

space.description: 'model' (design space, US survey feet) or a sheet id/name (paper space, inches), e.g. 'SH-004' or 'P-201'

layer.description: layer name; defaults to the current layer

kind.description: linear (measured along one axis), aligned (the true distance between two points), angular (the angle at a vertex), radius, diameter, or arc_length

line_point.description: where the dimension line goes -- the point a drafter drags to. It also settles what is being measured: clear above or below a pair of points is a horizontal dimension and out to the side a vertical one; on an angular dimension it picks which of the four angles between the rays is meant; on a radius or diameter it is where the text sits (inside the circle draws across it, outside draws a leader)

p1.description: first measured point (angular: a point out along the first ray; radius/diameter: the point on the circle the arrow touches, default: toward line_point)

p2.description: second measured point (arc_length: the far end, measured counter-clockwise from p1)

center.description: angular: the vertex. radius/diameter/arc_length: the centre of the circle

radius.description: radius of the circle being measured; or give of_entity

of_entity.description: measure this entity: a line/polyline/arc end to end (linear, aligned), or an arc/circle's own geometry (radius, diameter, arc_length). Ids come from find_entities and hit_test; reference elements are 'SURVEY:LN-001'

from_entity.description: measure from a point on this entity (angular: one of the two lines whose intersection is the vertex)

to_entity.description: measure to a point on this entity (angular: the other line)

from_at.description: where on from_entity: start|mid|end or a fraction 0-1 (default mid)

to_at.description: where on to_entity: start|mid|end or a fraction 0-1 (default mid)

rotation_deg.description: linear: the direction measured along (0 = horizontal, 90 = vertical). Omit and the engine reads it off line_point

text.description: override the measured value ('' hides the text entirely); omit to let the number follow the geometry

prefix.description: before the number; defaults to the kind's own (R=, Ø, L=)

unit_format.description: feet (120.00'), feet_inches (12'-6") or decimal (no unit mark). Default: feet in model space, decimal on a sheet. An angular dimension reads DMS (28°15'30") unless this is 'decimal'

arrow.description: terminator: arrow (default), tick (the oblique civil slash), dot, or none

arrow_size.description: arrowhead length (default 1.2 x the text height)

text_gap.description: gap between the dimension line and the text (default 0.5 x the text height)

extension_offset.description: gap between the measured point and its extension line (default 0.6 x the text height)

extension_beyond.description: how far an extension line runs past the dimension line (default 1.0 x the text height)

text_height.description: text height in space units; defaults to the annotation scale in model space, 0.10 in on a sheet

measure_scale.description: multiplier from drawn length to reported length (AutoCAD DIMLFAC). 1 by default; on a sheet, set it to the viewport's plot scale (50 for 1"=50') to dimension in model feet

Bearings run the way each line was drawn. Given a sheet as space, model linework is lettered on the sheet through its viewports, in paper inches.

ids.description: lines, polylines (each segment) and arcs to label -- right of way, easements, a deed's courses

style.description: values (default): bearing over distance along each line, radius and delta over length on each curve. tags: L1, C1 ... on the linework with a line table and a curve table listing the values

space.description: where the labels go (default where the linework is); a sheet letters model linework through its viewports, in paper inches
default where the tags go

offset.description: gap between the line and its labels (default 0.6 x the text height)

order_along.description: number and letter the segments in order of station along this alignment ('RTE-7', or a referenced 'BASE:RTE-7') instead of the order of ids

layer.description: layer name; defaults to the current layer

commands.description: Translate entities by [dx, dy].

commands.name: offset_entity
commands.description: Copy a line, polyline, arc or circle parallel to itself at a distance (AutoCAD OFFSET, MicroStation Copy Parallel): say the side as left/right of the direction it runs, or give a point on that side (toward) or one the copy passes through (through), or several signed offsets at once. Several entities that join end to end are offset together as one path, corners mitred (or rounded) so the copy stays continuous; curves keep their centre and change radius. Works on reference elements too, copying them into this document. For an alignment's own offsets, tied to the design, use draw_offset.

ids.description: what to copy parallel: one line, polyline, arc or circle, or several that join end to end (in order along them), offset together as one path. Reference elements ('BASE:LN-017') may be copied into this document

distance.description: how far, with side or toward

side.description: left or right of the direction the path runs: a line start to end, a polyline in vertex order, an arc or circle counter-clockwise, a chain in the order of ids

toward.description: a point on the side to offset to, the way a drafter clicks the side

through.description: a point the parallel passes through; the distance is measured square to the path

offsets.description: several parallels at once, right of the path's direction positive ('15L', '15R' say the side): [-15, 15] is both edges of a 30 ft pavement

join.description: outside corners: sharp extends the pieces to meet (default), round swings an arc about the corner

layer.description: layer of the copies; default the source's layer

color.description: named CAD color (black, red, yellow, green, cyan, blue, magenta, gray, white) or '#RRGGBB'

commands.name: fillet
commands.description: Round the corner between two lines with a curve of a given radius, tangent to both, and trim or extend the lines to meet it (AutoCAD FILLET, MicroStation Construct Circular Fillet) -- a curb return, a driveway flare, the corner of a parking area. The lines need not touch; keep says which part of each line stays when they cross. Radius 0 extends or trims them to a sharp corner. The answer gives the tangent points, delta, tangent length and arc length.

radius.description: curve radius; 0 extends or trims the lines to a sharp corner

keep.description: a point on the part of each line to keep, in the order of ids (where a drafter clicks them); default: each line's end farther from where they meet

trim.description: trim or extend the lines to the tangent points (default true); false draws only the curve

layer.description: layer of the curve; default the first line's

color.description: named CAD color (black, red, yellow, green, cyan, blue, magenta, gray, white) or '#RRGGBB'

commands.name: chamfer
commands.description: Cut the corner between two lines with a straight line, a distance back along each from where they meet, or a distance and an angle (AutoCAD CHAMFER, MicroStation Construct Chamfer) -- a corner cut-off, a building corner -- and trim the lines to it.

distance.description: how far back from the corner on the first line

distance2.description: how far back on the second (default distance)

angle.description: instead of distance2: the chamfer's angle from the first line

keep.description: a point on the part of each line to keep (default each line's end farther from the corner)

trim.description: trim the lines to the chamfer (default true)

layer.description: layer name; defaults to the current layer

commands.name: trim
commands.description: Cut linework back to where it crosses other linework (AutoCAD TRIM, MicroStation Trim to Element): each target names the entity and at, a point on the part to cut away (or keep, the part to keep). The cutting edges are every line, polyline, arc and circle in the space -- references included -- unless boundaries names them. Pavement edges drawn through a cul-de-sac bulb or past a cross street are trimmed this way; a circle cut twice becomes an arc. Design linework keeps its anchor, re-stationed.

id.description: the line, polyline, arc or circle to cut

at.description: a point on the part to cut away -- where a drafter clicks

keep.description: instead of at: a point on the part to keep; every other part goes

targets.description: what to trim, each with at (the part to remove) or keep (the part to keep). The entity is cut where the edges cross it

boundaries.description: the edges to cut or extend to (lines, polylines, arcs, circles; reference elements 'BASE:LN-017' count too). Omit to use every one in the space, as AutoCAD's quick trim does

extend_boundaries.description: count an edge where it would cross if it ran on (a line as its infinite line, an arc as its circle) -- AutoCAD's edge mode Extend (default false)

include_references.description: with no boundaries named: reference elements are edges too (default true)

commands.name: extend
commands.description: Run lines, arcs and open polylines on to the nearest boundary edge (AutoCAD EXTEND, MicroStation Extend Element to Intersection) -- a curb line to the cross street's edge. A line runs straight on, an arc round its circle; extend_boundaries also counts an edge where it would cross if it ran on.

id.description: the line, arc or open polyline to run on

at.description: instead of end: a point near the end to extend

targets.description: what to extend: each runs straight on (an arc round its circle) to the nearest edge

boundaries.description: the edges to cut or extend to (lines, polylines, arcs, circles; reference elements 'BASE:LN-017' count too). Omit to use every one in the space, as AutoCAD's quick trim does

extend_boundaries.description: count an edge where it would cross if it ran on (a line as its infinite line, an arc as its circle) -- AutoCAD's edge mode Extend (default false)

include_references.description: with no boundaries named: reference elements are edges too (default true)

commands.name: lengthen
commands.description: Change the length of a line, arc or open polyline at one end: by delta (negative shortens), to a total, by percent, or to where a point falls (AutoCAD LENGTHEN) -- 'extend the edge 25 ft', 'make the taper 120 ft long'.

at.description: instead of end: a point near the end that moves

delta.description: feet to add along it (negative shortens)

percent.description: the new length as a percentage of the old

to.description: run the end to where this point falls square to it

commands.name: break_entity
commands.description: Split an entity in two at a point, or cut out the part between two points (AutoCAD BREAK / BREAKATPOINT, MicroStation Partial Delete). A circle loses the part from at counter-clockwise to to and becomes an arc; a closed polyline opens.

at.description: where to break it (the nearest point on it)

to.description: a second point: the part between at and to is removed (on a circle or closed polyline, from at onward to to). Without it the entity is split in two at at

commands.name: join_entities
commands.description: Join pieces into one (AutoCAD JOIN / PEDIT Join, MicroStation Create Complex Chain): collinear lines into one line, arcs on one circle into one arc (a circle when they close it), and anything that meets end to end into one polyline that keeps its arcs as arc segments -- a curb line drawn in pieces becomes one thing to offset, measure or hatch.

ids.description: lines, arcs and polylines to join: collinear lines become one line and arcs on one circle one arc (across gaps); anything else that meets end to end becomes one polyline, arcs kept as arc segments (closed when it closes)

tolerance.description: largest gap between ends that still join (default 0.01)

commands.name: explode_entities
commands.description: Take compound entities apart (AutoCAD EXPLODE, MicroStation Drop Element): a polyline into lines and arcs, a block reference into what the block is drawn with, a dimension or table into lines and text, a point into its marker and label, a hatch into its boundary polylines.

ids.description: polylines (into lines and arcs), block references (into what the block is drawn with), dimensions and tables (into lines and text), points (marker and label) and hatches (into their boundary polylines)

commands.name: copy_entities
commands.description: Copy entities by a displacement -- delta, or from a base point to another -- count times over (AutoCAD COPY, MicroStation Copy Element). Reference elements are copied into this document. Copies are drawing, not design: no anchor, and COGO points get new numbers.

ids.description: what to copy; reference elements are copied into this document

count.description: repeat the displacement this many times (default 1)

commands.name: rotate_entities
commands.description: Rotate entities about a base point by an angle (degrees counter-clockwise), or turn one direction onto another -- 'turn the building so this side runs N 34°15'00" E' (AutoCAD ROTATE Reference, MicroStation Rotate). copy=true rotates a copy.

angle.description: degrees counter-clockwise (DMS text works; '30 CW' turns clockwise)

from_direction.description: with to_direction: turn this direction onto that one (AutoCAD rotate reference) -- e.g. a building's side given by two corners onto a bearing

to_direction.description: a direction: a quadrant bearing ("N 30°00'00\" E"), an azimuth ('AZ 30'), or two points [[x1, y1], [x2, y2]] along it

copy.description: rotate a copy, leaving the original (default false)

commands.name: mirror_entities

line.description: two points on the mirror line

keep_original.description: keep the original and add the mirror image (default true); false mirrors in place. Text stays readable

commands.name: scale_entities
commands.description: Scale entities about a base point by a factor, or so one length becomes another (AutoCAD SCALE Reference, MicroStation Scale). copy=true scales a copy.

from_length.description: with to_length: scale so this length becomes that one

model_center.description: model-space point (feet) shown at the viewport center

rotation_deg.description: view twist: model appears rotated CCW by this angle on the sheet

commands.name: modify_viewport

commands.description: Set title block fields on a sheet.

A key the border does not letter is kept with the sheet, and the result warns; get_sheet_state lists a sheet's own (title_block_keys)

commands.name: annotate_stationing
commands.description: The roadway stationing engine. Entity-chain mode (path_ids + begin_station): walk connected line/polyline/arc entities. Design mode (alignment=NAME): use the alignment's true stations and equations and anchor every tick and label. Either way it draws perpendicular ticks at the interval, '84+27.93' labels rotated along the path, and BC/EC/PCC/PRC labels at the curve points.

space.description: 'model' (design space, US survey feet) or a sheet id/name (paper space, inches), e.g. 'SH-004' or 'P-201'

path_ids.description: line/polyline/arc entity ids forming the centerline, in order along it (entity-chain mode); with chain=true, any one or more of them

chain.description: entity-chain mode: follow the elements joined end to end from path_ids, so one id stations the whole centerline; stops where the linework branches, unless path_ids names the way on

alignment.description: design-model alignment name: true stations, equations, and anchored output (alternative to path_ids); a referenced one as 'BASE:ALIGN-1'

lettering.description: alignment mode: 'caltrans' (default) letters the whole station number at each 500 ft and the ones digit elsewhere (85, 6, 7, ... 90); 'full' letters every station 86+00.00

station_side.description: alignment mode: where the station numbers go; default below the line

point_side.description: alignment mode: where the BC/EC and equation lettering goes, square to the line and reading bottom to top; default left

view_rotation.description: alignment mode: the twist (rotation_deg) of the viewport the labels are read through; they are lettered upright on that sheet instead of in the model (default 0, an untwisted view)

point_label_offset.description: alignment mode: BC/EC and equation distance from the line (default 22.5 ft, or the annotation scale x 0.45 in)

begin_station.description: entity-chain mode: the station (feet, or '15+90.29') at the start of the first element, or at start_point when given

start_point.description: entity-chain mode: a point on the path where begin_station is known; stations run on from the end of the path nearer it

reverse.description: entity-chain mode: run the stations the other way along the path

station_range.description: alignment mode: only annotate between these display stations

include_equations.description: alignment mode: label station equations (default true)

tick_half_len.description: tick half-length each side of the path (default 3.5 ft, a 7 ft tick at 1" = 50', or the annotation scale x 0.07 in)

text_height.description: label height (default 8 ft, or the annotation scale x 0.10 in)

label_offset.description: station number distance from the path, below it (default 6 ft, or the annotation scale x 0.12 in: half a text height under the tick); negative is the older way of asking for stations on the right, BC/EC left

layer.description: layer for ticks; default current

label_layer.description: layer for labels; default same as ticks

include_pc_pt.description: letter BC/EC/PCC/PRC at the curve points (default true)

connect_tolerance.description: max gap between path elements (default 1 ft)

commands.name: place_along
commands.description: Place a symbol (a block) or COGO points along a path -- a line, a chain or an alignment -- every so many feet (AutoCAD MEASURE) or a count of them evenly spaced (DIVIDE), on it or offset square to it: delineators every 200 ft 2 ft outside the edge, guard rail posts, station markers. On an alignment the positions fall on round stations; blocks turn with the path.

path.description: what to run along: an entity id (line, polyline, arc, circle; reference elements too), a list of ids that join end to end, or an alignment of this document ('ALIGN-1')

every.description: spacing along the path, feet in model. On an alignment with no from, positions fall on round stations (every 100 -> 81+00, 82+00, ...)

count.description: how many, evenly spaced from from to to, both ends included (AutoCAD DIVIDE)

from.description: where to start: distance along the path, or on an alignment a station ('82+00'); default its start

to.description: where to stop (distance or station); default its end

offset.description: square off the path, right of its direction positive ('2R', '2L' say the side); default on it

block.description: insert this block at each position (delineators, signs, markers); default COGO points

align.description: turn blocks to the path's direction (default true)

rotation.description: extra rotation of each block, degrees CCW

start_number.description: points: first number (default the next free)

size.description: marker width in space units (default the label height)

text_height.description: label height in space units (default 0.08 in on paper: 0.08 x the annotation scale in model)

label.description: label lines beside the marker, top to bottom (default number, elevation, description; [] for none)

layer.description: layer name; defaults to the current layer

commands.name: create_alignment
commands.description: Create a horizontal alignment in the design model from PIs ([x, y] at BEGIN/END, [x, y, R] interior), from bearings and distances (start + legs: each leg a bearing, azimuth or deflection and the distance to the next PI, with the radius of the curve at the PI it starts from), or from CoordGeom elements; optional begin station (display, '80+00') and station equations. x is the easting and y the northing, so N 7300, E 4100 is [4100, 7300]. Given legs, the engine computes the PIs -- no trigonometry by hand -- and get_design_data kind=tangents reads the bearings and lengths back. Alignments are pure design data: draw_alignment puts linework in model space, annotate_stationing/place_label label it.

start.description: BEGIN, where legs start: [x, y] = [easting, northing]

items.description: one tangent, from one PI to the next: a direction (exactly one of bearing, azimuth, deflection, angle_right) and the distance to the next PI; radius is the curve at the PI where this leg starts (a leg after the first). Or as text: "S 76°15'00\" E 650", "33 L 820 R=450"

bearing.description: quadrant bearing: N 47°30'15" E, S47-30-15W, N47E

deflection.description: the angle the alignment turns at the PI where this leg starts: '33 L', '18°30'00" RT', or a number with right positive; or its size with turn

distance.description: feet from this leg's PI to the next PI

radius.description: the curve at the PI where this leg starts (0 or omitted: none, which needs angle_points)

legs.description: the layout as bearings and distances, PI to PI from start -- as a report describes it: 'S 76° E 650 ft to PI-2, where it deflects 33° left on a 450 ft curve; then 820 ft...' is [{bearing: 'S 76 E', distance: 650}, {deflection: '33 L', radius: 450, distance: 820}, ...]

angle_points.description: allow interior PIs of radius 0: angle points, where the tangents meet with no curve -- a layout whose curves come later (default false: a missing radius is refused)

commands.name: modify_alignment
commands.description: Change an alignment's PIs, begin station, equations, description, or name (rename rewrites anchors and profile bindings). The labels lettered from it follow the new design (update_labels); its drawn linework does not: redraw=true redraws the centerline, draw_offset replace=true the offsets (a warning names what is left).

changes.description: any of: pis, begin_station, equations, description, rename

angle_points.description: allow interior PIs of radius 0: angle points, where the tangents meet with no curve -- a layout whose curves come later (default false: a missing radius is refused)

redraw.description: when the pis change, redraw the alignment's drawn elements to the new geometry, on the layer they were drawn on (default false)

commands.name: update_labels
commands.description: Bring the labels lettered from an alignment up to date with its design: place_label labels move to their anchors and re-letter, annotate_stationing sets are laid out again (new stations ticked, stations past a new end dropped), curve tables refill. modify_alignment does this for this document's own alignments; run it after the basefile a referenced alignment ('BASE:RTE-7') lives in has changed. Labels whose anchor is gone are named, not deleted. No alignment: every one with labels.

alignment.description: the alignment whose labels to bring up to date: this document's, or a referenced one as 'BASE:RTE-7'; omit for every one

commands.name: delete_alignment
commands.description: Delete an alignment (cascade=true also deletes its profiles); drawn entities keep their anchors.

cascade.description: also delete profiles bound to it (default false)

commands.name: create_profile
commands.description: Create a vertical profile on an alignment from PVIs ([station, elevation] or [station, elevation, vc_length]; stations are display stations).

commands.name: delete_profile
commands.description: Delete a profile by name.

commands.name: draw_alignment
commands.description: Draw an alignment's tangents and curves as anchored line/arc entities in model space (replace=true redraws).

color.description: named CAD color (black, red, yellow, green, cyan, blue, magenta, gray, white) or '#RRGGBB'

replace.description: delete this alignment's previously drawn elements first (default false)

commands.name: draw_offset
commands.description: Draw constant offsets of an alignment as anchored lines and arcs: pavement edges, shoulders, right of way. Offsets are feet, right of the direction of stationing positive ('15L' says the side out loud), so a 30 ft pavement is offsets [-15, 15]. Tangents shift sideways; curves keep their center and change radius, so the chain meets end to end exactly. station_range draws only part of the chain, which is how an edge or a curb line stops short of an intersection and picks up again on the far leg.

offsets.description: offset distances from the alignment, feet, right of the direction of stationing positive; a string may name the side ('15L', '15R'). A 30 ft pavement is [-15, 15]; add [-21, 21] for 6 ft shoulders.

station_range.description: draw only between these display stations: how a pavement edge stops at an intersection and picks up again on the far leg

color.description: named CAD color (black, red, yellow, green, cyan, blue, magenta, gray, white) or '#RRGGBB'

replace.description: delete this alignment's previously drawn offsets at the same distances first (default false); with a station_range, only the pieces inside it

commands.name: draw_station_offset
commands.description: Draw linework through station-and-offset points of an alignment ('82+00@15R', 'PC-2@15L', 'END@18R') -- Civil 3D's transparent station-offset ('SO) with no coordinates worked out by hand. Where consecutive points share an offset the run follows the alignment exactly (arcs on its curves, anchored like draw_offset); where the offset changes it is a straight taper. A turn lane is one call: ['82+00@15R', '82+90@26R', '86+50@26R', '86+50@15R'].

space.description: model (the default; stations are model feet)

alignment.description: the alignment the stations are on (default the only one)

items.description: BEGIN | END | PI-n | PC-n | PT-n | MC-n | T-n | EQ-n | '86+50.00' | 8650, optionally '@offset' (ft, right +, e.g. 'PC-2@18', '86+50@25L'); or {ref|station, offset, region}. BC-n and EC-n, as a Caltrans plan letters them, are PC-n and PT-n

follow.description: between two points at the same offset, follow the alignment (arcs on its curves, exactly as draw_offset) instead of a straight chord (default true); where the offset changes the run is a straight taper

polyline.description: draw one polyline (curves as arc segments) instead of lines and arcs

close.description: close back to the first point

layer.description: layer name; defaults to the current layer

commands.name: place_label
commands.description: Place a design-anchored label: name a point on an alignment (PC-2, T-3, '86+50@25L', ...) and a kind (station, pc, pt, pi, mc, bearing, equation, curve_data, custom...); content, side, offset, and rotation follow drafting convention unless overridden. Works in model space or on a sheet through a viewport. The text records its anchor for the verifier.

space.description: 'model' (design space, US survey feet) or a sheet id/name (paper space, inches), e.g. 'SH-004' or 'P-201'

alignment.description: this document's alignment, or a referenced one as 'BASE:ALIGN-1' (read through the attachment, which must sit at identity)

anchor.description: BEGIN | END | PI-n | PC-n | PT-n | MC-n | T-n | EQ-n | '86+50.00' | 8650, optionally '@offset' (ft, right +, e.g. 'PC-2@18', '86+50@25L'); or {ref|station, offset, region}. BC-n and EC-n, as a Caltrans plan letters them, are PC-n and PT-n

content.description: explicit text; omit to auto-generate from design data the Caltrans way (recorded either way): '84+62.18 BC', 'N 63°12'40" E 911.47'', the curve number '1' in a bubble with a leader

side.description: left/right of the stationing direction, or above/below on the paper (resolved to the line's left or right and recorded so); default by kind: station numbers below, bearings above, curve points and equations left, the curve bubble right

label_offset.description: distance from the anchor point, feet in model / inches on sheets; default by kind, sized for 1" = 50' in model: stations 6 ft / 0.12 in, bearings 3 ft / 0.06 in, curve points and equations 22.5 ft / 0.45 in, the curve bubble 40 ft / 0.80 in

rotation.description: default by kind: curve points and equations perpendicular (reading bottom to top), the curve number horizontal, the rest along the line

height.description: text height, feet in model / inches on sheets; default 8 ft / 0.10 in

view_rotation.description: model space: the twist (rotation_deg) of the viewport the labels are read through; they are lettered upright on that sheet instead of in the model (default 0, an untwisted view)

color.description: named CAD color (black, red, yellow, green, cyan, blue, magenta, gray, white) or '#RRGGBB'

viewport.description: sheet space only: viewport id/name carrying the anchor; default = the first viewport whose frame contains the point

commands.name: place_curve_table
commands.description: Place a curve data table (Δ, R, T, L, chord, bearings...) for an alignment on a sheet, one row per curve, anchored to the alignment.

space.description: 'model' (design space, US survey feet) or a sheet id/name (paper space, inches), e.g. 'SH-004' or 'P-201'

alignment.description: this document's alignment, or a referenced one as 'BASE:ALIGN-1'

curves.description: the curves this sheet shows, by the alignment's own curve index (C-1, C-2 ...); default all

first_curve_number.description: the plan's number for the alignment's first curve (default 1): curve numbers run along the line and never restart on the next sheet, so a design holding a later part of the line numbers on from the sheet before

columns.description: keys: curve, pi_sta, pc_sta, pt_sta, delta, direction, radius, tangent, length, external, mid_ordinate, chord, chord_bearing; default the Caltrans table: curve, radius, delta, tangent, length (No., R, Δ, T, L)

color.description: named CAD color (black, red, yellow, green, cyan, blue, magenta, gray, white) or '#RRGGBB'

commands.name: import_landxml
commands.description: Import LandXML 1.2 alignments (Line/Curve CoordGeom, station equations) and profiles into the design model, from a file path (read at execute time, so replay depends on the file) or inline xml text.

path.description: path to a LandXML 1.2 file, read when the command executes (replaying the journal then depends on the file, like attach_reference)

xml.description: LandXML text inline (keeps the journal self-contained)

commands.name: attach_reference
commands.description: Attach an external RoadDraft document (basefile) as a reference (AutoCAD: xref, MicroStation: reference attachment). The host stores path + placement + display settings; the basefile's model geometry displays under this document's own entities and in sheet viewports, and reloads from disk — never copied in. Relative paths resolve against the host document's folder. true_scale converts the basefile's units into the host space's (default on); levels_off, symbology (color/linetype/lineweight_mm/gray), clip (boundary polygon) and masks (mask polygons) control how it displays; model picks the basefile's design model or one of its sheets; nest_depth shows the basefile's own references (live nesting).

path.description: path to a RoadDraft document (.rdraft or .rdoc.json, saved with save_document); a relative path resolves against the host document's folder, then the working directory

space.description: 'model' (design space, US survey feet) or a sheet id/name (paper space, inches), e.g. 'SH-004' or 'P-201'

true_scale.description: convert the basefile's model_units into the host space's units before placement (default true; MicroStation true scale)

levels_off.description: basefile layers (levels) hidden in this attachment only

symbology.description: display overrides for the whole attachment: color, linetype, lineweight_mm, gray (true = gray-out)

clip.description: clip boundary polygon in host coordinates; only basefile geometry inside it displays

items.description: polygon: at least 3 [x, y] points, implicitly closed

masks.description: clip mask polygons in host coordinates; geometry inside a mask is hidden

model.description: which basefile model to attach: 'model' (its design model, default) or one of its sheet names/ids (paper inches, border and title block included)

nest_depth.description: live nesting: also display the basefile's own references this many levels deep (default 0 = none)

commands.name: detach_reference
commands.description: Detach a reference by name.

commands.name: modify_reference
commands.description: Change a reference's path, placement (offset/rotation/scale), visibility, true_scale, per-attachment level display (levels_off), symbology overrides (color, linetype, lineweight_mm, gray=true for gray-out), clip boundary (clip: polygon in host coordinates, null clears), clip masks (masks: list of polygons), model (design model or a basefile sheet) or nest_depth (live nesting).

changes.description: any of: path, offset, rotation_deg, scale, visible, true_scale, levels_off (list of basefile layer names), symbology ({color, linetype, lineweight_mm, gray}), clip (polygon in host coordinates, or null to clear), masks (list of polygons), model ('model' or a basefile sheet), nest_depth (0-5)

commands.name: reload_references
commands.description: Re-read all referenced basefiles from disk on next use; warns when labels lettered through a reference no longer match its design (update_labels).

commands.name: set_annotation_scale
commands.description: Set the current annotation scale (AutoCAD annotation scale / Civil 3D drawing scale): annotation commands then size text, ticks and label offsets from paper defaults (0.10 / 0.20 / 0.32 in) x the scale, stamp what they draw as annotative, and this command re-sizes existing annotative model annotation for the new plot scale (anchored labels are re-placed through the design). null/'off' restores the fixed feet defaults.

scale.description: a scale-list name ('1"=50''), feet per inch (50), '1:600', or null/'off' to turn annotation scaling off

rescale.description: re-size existing annotative model entities to the new scale (default true)

adopt.description: also stamp un-scaled model texts and anchored ticks as annotative at the new scale (default false)

commands.name: add_annotation_scale
commands.description: Add a named plot scale to the document's scale list.

commands.name: delete_annotation_scale
commands.description: Remove a plot scale from the scale list (not the current one).

scale.description: list name or feet per inch

commands.name: set_annotation_defaults
commands.description: Set the paper-unit annotation defaults (text height, tick half-length, label offset in inches) that the annotation scale converts to feet.

label_offset_in.description: label offset from the line on paper (default 0.32)

commands.name: undo
commands.description: Revert the most recent command.

commands.name: redo
commands.description: Re-apply the most recently undone command.

queries.name: get_document_state
queries.description: Document state. detail='summary' (default) for counts and resource lists; detail='full' for the complete document JSON (every entity, layer, style, block, sheet).

queries.name: get_model_state
queries.description: All model-space entities as JSON, optionally filtered to a bounding box (feet). include_references=true also lists what the attachments show, read-only, in host coordinates and addressed 'REFNAME:ID' -- which is how to find geometry to annotate in a sheet file whose design is referenced in.

queries.name: find_entities
queries.description: Find entities by what they are rather than where they are: layer, type, anchor (alignment / kind / ref / offset), text content, a bounding box, or what a given sheet shows. Any filter takes one value or a list of values (match any). Searches attached references too, so it is how to locate geometry in a sheet file whose design is referenced in. Each row carries a point that is ON the entity, ready to pass to place_callout as target_entity or target.

space.description: space to search (default 'model')

layer.description: layer name, or a list of them

anchor.description: match the design anchor: any of alignment, kind (element|offset|station|tick|pc|pt|...), ref, offset. Each takes one value or a list, so {kind: 'offset', offset: [-15, 15]} finds both pavement edges.

content_contains.description: text entities whose content contains this (case-insensitive)

visible_on.description: sheet name: keep only model entities that sheet's viewports actually show. Each row then also carries sheet_point -- the middle of the part shown, in paper inches -- and the viewport it is seen through

detail.description: summary (default) is id, type, layer, a point on the entity, its length and anchor; full adds the whole entity

queries.name: point_on_entity
queries.description: A point that is genuinely ON an entity, and the direction it runs there: where='start'|'mid'|'end' or a fraction from 0 to 1. Use it instead of computing a point from an arc's center and angles -- the midpoint of a curve's endpoints is not on the curve. Works on reference elements ('BASE:AR-009'). With sheet, 'where' runs along the part of the entity that sheet shows and the answer adds where it falls on the paper -- the same point place_callout aims at from that sheet.

sheet.description: a sheet that sees this model entity through a viewport

queries.name: model_to_sheet
queries.description: Where a model point falls on a sheet, in paper inches, seen through a viewport's centre, scale and twist. Use it to decide where annotation text should sit -- never do the viewport arithmetic by hand. visible=false means no viewport shows the point (the mapping through the first or given viewport is still returned). To aim a callout, skip this and give place_callout a target_entity or target_anchor.

queries.name: sheet_to_model
queries.description: What a point on a sheet's paper is looking at: the model point under it through the viewport it falls in, and the nearest entity there (references included) with its distance in feet. inside=false means the point is outside every viewport window.

queries.name: measure
queries.description: Measure without drawing (AutoCAD DIST / MEASUREGEOM): the distance, dx/dy, bearing and azimuth between two points, or one entity's own length, radius and sweep. 'from' and 'to' each take a point or an entity id (with from_at/to_at: start|mid|end or a fraction), so a curve is measured from a point genuinely on it. With along -- a line, a chain of entities or an alignment -- the points are measured relative to it instead (MicroStation Measure Distance along an element / perpendicular): how far along it each one falls and how far off it, square, left or right; with two points, the distance between them along it and across it. The formatted reading is the same string place_dimension would draw, which makes it the way to check a dimension before or after placing it.

from.description: a point [x, y] or an entity id

to.description: a point [x, y] or an entity id

along.description: measure relative to this: an entity id (line, polyline, arc, circle; reference elements 'BASE:LN-017'), a list of ids that join end to end, or an alignment name ('RTE-7', 'BASE:RTE-7'). Each point is projected square onto it: along = distance from its start (the station, on an alignment), offset = perpendicular distance, right of its direction positive

entity.description: measure this entity on its own: length, and for an arc or circle its centre, radius and sweep

queries.name: traverse
queries.description: Coordinate geometry without drawing: from a start point (or the end of an entity) run courses by bearing, azimuth or deflection and distance, and curve courses by radius and delta, length or chord, and get back every point, bearing and length -- point + bearing + distance -> point, with no trigonometry by hand. close=true adds the misclosure of a boundary and its precision (1:N). draw_traverse draws the same courses; create_alignment takes start + legs directly.

start.description: where the traverse begins: a point [x, y] (x = easting, y = northing), or an entity id to continue from its end (start_at says which end; the entity's direction there is the course a leading deflection turns from)

start_at.description: with a start entity: continue from its end (default) or its start

items.description: one course. Straight: a direction (exactly one of bearing, azimuth, deflection, angle_right) and distance. Curve: radius, turn and one of delta, length or chord; it continues the previous course's direction unless chord_bearing places it (a non-tangent curve). Or the course as text: "N 47°30'15\" E 250", "AZ 75.5 250", "33 L 820", "CURVE R=450 LEFT DELTA=33"

bearing.description: quadrant bearing: N 47°30'15" E, S47-30-15W, N47E

azimuth.description: degrees clockwise from north, 0-360 (a number or DMS text)

deflection.description: the angle turned from the previous course, with its side: '33 L', '18°30'00" RT', or a number with right (clockwise) positive; or its size with turn

turn.description: which way a deflection or a curve turns

angle_right.description: angle measured clockwise from the backsight (the previous course run backwards), as a field traverse records it

distance.description: length of a straight course (feet in model)

radius.description: radius of a curve course -- giving one makes the course a curve

chord_bearing.description: a non-tangent curve's chord bearing (or azimuth)

legs.description: the courses in order, each from where the last one ended

initial_bearing.description: the direction a leading deflection or tangent curve turns from, as a quadrant bearing

close.description: the traverse should close on its start: report the misclosure (distance, bearing, precision 1:N) and, when drawing, add the closing course

queries.name: key_points
queries.description: The exact points a drafter snaps to, listed: endpoints and vertices, midpoints, centers, quadrants, insertion points, dimension definition points (node), intersections between the entities, and the design points of alignments (BEGIN, PI, BC/PC, EC/PT, radius points, END -- points with no entity at them, each carrying the anchor that names it). Name entities (id / ids), an alignment, or a space and bounds. Use the points directly instead of computing a corner or a curve's end by hand.

ids.description: several entities; their intersections with each other are listed too

alignment.description: an alignment's design points ('RTE-7', or a referenced 'BASE:RTE-7')

space.description: with no ids: every entity in this space (default model)

include_references.description: with no ids: attachments too (default true)

queries.name: snap
queries.description: Object snap: the exact key point nearest a rough point, as a cursor snaps in CAD -- endpoint, midpoint, center, quadrant, intersection, insertion, node, design (alignment PI/BC/EC...), and with 'from' (the point a line is drawn from) perpendicular and tangent; nearest is the fallback when nothing else is in reach. On a sheet it also snaps through the viewport to the model and its references, answering in paper inches with the model point beside it.

space.description: space to snap in (default model)

tolerance.description: how far to look, in space units (default 5 ft in model, 0.1 in on a sheet)

modes.description: snap modes to use (default endpoint, midpoint, center, intersection, perpendicular, insertion, design)

from.description: the point the line is being drawn from, for perpendicular and tangent

viewport.description: on a sheet: snap through this viewport

queries.name: get_sheet_state
queries.description: One sheet: size, usable area, title block fields and the keys its border letters (title_block_keys), viewports (with the model region each shows), entities.

queries.name: get_entity
queries.description: One entity by id, with its space, bounding box and properties -- what AutoCAD's LIST reads off it: a line's length and bearing, a curve's radius, delta, length, chord and tangent, a polyline's segments (and area when closed), a circle's area, a point's northing, easting and elevation, a hatch's area. Reference elements are addressed as 'REFNAME:ID' (as returned by hit_test) and come back in host coordinates, read-only.

queries.name: area
queries.description: Area and perimeter without drawing anything (AutoCAD AREA, MicroStation Measure Area): of closed entities or entities that join into closed loops (ids; a loop inside another is an island and subtracts), a hatch, a polygon of points, or the region of linework around a point (at) -- the area a pick-a-point hatch would fill. Square feet, square yards and acres in model space (square inches on a sheet), with the centroid and each loop's figures.

ids.description: closed entities (closed polylines, circles, hatches) or entities that join end to end into closed loops

at.description: a point inside linework that closes around it

space.description: with points or at: the space (default model)

islands.description: with at: closed shapes inside subtract (default true)

gap_tolerance.description: largest gap that still closes a loop (default 0.01)

boundary_layers.description: with at: only linework on these layers

include_references.description: with at: reference linework too (default true)

queries.name: get_extents
queries.description: Bounding box of all entities in a space.

queries.name: list_layers
queries.description: All layers with color/linetype/lineweight/visibility.

queries.name: list_text_styles
queries.description: All text styles.

queries.name: list_blocks
queries.description: All block (cell) definitions.

queries.name: list_sheets
queries.description: All sheets with sizes and entity/viewport counts.

queries.name: list_references
queries.description: All attached references (basefiles) with placement, load status, resolved path, unit handling (true scale factor), per-level display, symbology and clip settings.

queries.name: hit_test
queries.description: Find entities near a point (screen picking / locate). Returns nearest first, within tolerance (space units). Elements of attached references are located too (id 'REFNAME:ID', reference=name, read_only=true) unless include_references is false.

queries.name: get_journal
queries.description: The command journal (the session's action trajectory).

queries.name: list_commands
queries.description: The full tool manifest: every command and query with params schema, example, and C3D/ORD dialect aliases.

queries.name: render_sheet
queries.description: Render a sheet to PNG at true paper size (the vision observation). Returns the file path; set include_base64 for inline image data.

queries.name: render_model
queries.description: Render model space to PNG (design geometry only, no sheet frame).

queries.name: export_dxf
queries.description: Export the document as DXF (opens in AutoCAD/Civil 3D and MicroStation: real layers, blocks, layouts, viewports).

queries.name: export_pdf
queries.description: Export sheets to a multi-page PDF at paper size.

queries.name: print_pdf
queries.description: Print (plot) to PDF with page setup -- the PLOT dialog, where export_pdf is a batch dump. Prints one space (space='model' or a sheet), a set of sheets, or every sheet, onto the paper you choose at the scale you choose: fit-to-page, a half-size set (scale='1:2' on a sheet), or an exact plot scale in model space (scale=50 is 1"=50'). Also margins, portrait/landscape and monochrome. A print that would not fit the paper fails with the scale that would. Returns the path and what each page was plotted at.

space.description: 'model' (design space, US survey feet) or a sheet id/name (paper space, inches), e.g. 'SH-004' or 'P-201'

sheets.description: several sheets in one job; omit space and sheets to print every sheet

paper.description: paper to print on. 'sheet' (the default for a sheet) keeps the sheet's own size; model space needs a named paper and defaults to ANSI_D

orientation.description: turns a named paper; a sheet printed on its own size keeps its own orientation

scale.description: 'fit' (default) fits the page. On a sheet: printed inches per sheet inch -- 1 / '1:1' full size, 0.5 / '1:2' / '50%' a half-size set. In model space: feet per inch -- 50, '1"=50'' or '1:600'

bounds.description: model-space window to print (plot 'Window'); defaults to the extents

margin_in.description: unprintable margin on all four sides (default 0)

scale_lineweights.description: shrink lineweights with the plot scale (off, as in CAD)

queries.name: save_document
queries.description: Save the document. A path with no RoadDraft extension gets '.rdraft', the application document; '.rdoc.json' is the same JSON under the interchange name. The saved path is returned.

queries.name: save_journal
queries.description: Save the command journal (baseline + commands) as JSONL; replayable deterministically.

queries.name: list_alignments
queries.description: Every alignment in the design model: stations, length, curve/tangent/equation counts, bound profiles, and whether it has been drawn. include_references=true also lists the alignments inside attached basefiles, named 'REFNAME:ALIGNMENT' and read-only -- in a sheet file whose design is referenced in, that is the only place they are.

queries.name: station_to_xy
queries.description: Model-space point at a display station (+ offset, right positive) on an alignment, with heading, bearing, and the element it lands on (an exact junction reads the ahead element). An alignment in an attached basefile is named 'REFNAME:ALIGNMENT' (list_alignments include_references=true shows them); its points come back in host coordinates, while stations, lengths and bearings are as designed.

sheet.description: also say where this falls on that sheet: adds on_sheet {viewport, sheet_point in paper inches, visible}

queries.name: xy_to_station
queries.description: Perpendicular projection of a model-space point onto an alignment: station, offset (L/R), and the element. The point is given in host coordinates. An alignment in an attached basefile is named 'REFNAME:ALIGNMENT' (list_alignments include_references=true shows them); its points come back in host coordinates, while stations, lengths and bearings are as designed.

queries.name: resolve_anchor
queries.description: Dry run of place_label: where a label of this kind at this anchor would land (content, position, rotation, viewport) without placing it. Same faults as the command. For a referenced alignment ('BASE:RTE-7') it answers where the anchor is and what a label there would read, but not a label plan -- nothing can be anchored to an alignment this document does not own.

anchor.description: BEGIN | END | PI-n | PC-n | PT-n | MC-n | T-n | EQ-n | '86+50.00' | 8650, optionally '@offset' (ft, right +, e.g. 'PC-2@18', '86+50@25L'); or {ref|station, offset, region}. BC-n and EC-n, as a Caltrans plan letters them, are PC-n and PT-n

space.description: 'model' (design space, US survey feet) or a sheet id/name (paper space, inches), e.g. 'SH-004' or 'P-201'

side.description: left/right of the stationing direction, or above/below on the paper (resolved to the line's left or right and recorded so); default by kind: station numbers below, bearings above, curve points and equations left, the curve bubble right

sheet.description: for a referenced alignment: also say where the anchor falls on that sheet (on_sheet)

queries.name: get_design_data
queries.description: Tabular design data: alignments, curves (Δ/R/T/L/E/M/C, bearings, PC/PI/PT/MC stations), tangents, station equations, named anchors, profiles, PVIs, vertical curves. Stations are raw + display text. Paginated (default 50). kind defaults to 'alignments', the overview. An alignment in an attached basefile is named 'REFNAME:ALIGNMENT' (list_alignments include_references=true shows them); its points come back in host coordinates, while stations, lengths and bearings are as designed. A profile in one is named 'REFNAME:PROFILE' (the profiles list_alignments shows on a referenced alignment); profile alone reads it, or give the referenced alignment and the profile's own name.

queries.name: list_annotation_scales
queries.description: The annotation scale list, the current scale, the paper-unit defaults with their model equivalents, and how many model entities are annotative.

queries.name: export_landxml
queries.description: Export the design model (alignments + profiles) as LandXML 1.2 (USSurveyFoot); opens in Civil 3D / ORD.
